rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وموسى بن جعفر عن أبيه، وعلي بن الحسين، وقتادة، وأبو العالية، ومحمد بن يحيى بن حبان
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Musa b. Ja'far from his father, Ali b. al-Husayn, Qatada, Abu al-Aliya and Muhammad b. Yahya b. Habban hold that al-Fatiha is Meccan; 15:87 supports this because al-Hijr is unanimously Meccan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ، وموسى بن جعفر عن أبيه ، وعلي بن الحسين ، وقتادة ، وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy's report identifies al-Fatiha as the seven oft-repeated; the seven long surahs were revealed some time after al-Hijr, supporting a Meccan dating.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث أُبَيّ بن كعب أنها السبع المثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer became obligatory in Mecca, and no report preserves a Muslim prayer without reciting al-Fatiha; this supports its Meccan origin.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن فرض الصلاة كان بمكة ، وما حفظ أنها كانت قط

rows.speaker: عطاء بن يسار، وسوادة بن زياد، والزهري محمد بن مسلم، وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ata b. Yasar, Sawada b. Ziyad, al-Zuhri and Abd Allah b. Ubayd b. Umayr instead regard al-Fatiha as Medinan.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عطاء بن يسار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no disagreement that the surah is called Fatihat al-Kitab because its position makes it the opening of the Book.
rows.anchor: وأما أسماؤها فلا خلاف أنها يقال لها فاتحة الكتاب ، لأن موضعها يعطي ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan b. Abi al-Hasan objects to the title Umm al-Kitab, reserving that name for the lawful and unlawful, as in 3:7.
rows.anchor: فكره الحسن بن أبي الحسن ذلك وقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others accept Umm al-Kitab as a name for al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari explains the title Umm al-Kitab by al-Fatiha being written first in the codex and recited first in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال البخاري : سميت أم الكتاب لأنها يبدأ بكتابتها في المصحف وبقراءتها في الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin disliked calling al-Fatiha Umm al-Quran.
rows.anchor: فكره ذلك ابن سيرين وجوزه جمهور العلماء

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority of scholars permit the title Umm al-Quran, contrary to Ibn Sirin's dislike.
rows.anchor: فكره ذلك ابن سيرين وجوزه جمهور العلماء

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya b. Ya'mar analogizes Umm al-Quran to Umm al-Qura for Mecca and Umm Khurasan for Merv.
rows.anchor: قال يحيى بن يعمر : «أم القرى

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan b. Abi al-Hasan also gives al-Fatiha the name Umm al-Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن : اسمها أم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of al-Mathani is that the surah is repeated in every prayer cycle.
rows.anchor: فقيل سميت بذلك لأنها تثنى في كل ركعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that al-Fatiha was reserved as a treasure for this community and had not been revealed to anyone before it.
rows.anchor: وقيل سميت بذلك لأنها استثنيت لهذه الأمة فلم تنزل على أحد قبلها ذخرا لها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ubayy that no comparable surah had been revealed in the Torah, Gospel or Qur'an.
rows.anchor: في حديث أُبَيّ بن كعب «إنها لم ينزل في التوراة ولا في الإنجيل

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unnamed report says al-Fatiha is equivalent to two-thirds of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنها تعدل ثلثي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported equivalence may reflect the surah's meanings or be a divine preference not rationally explained; similar equivalences are reported for al-Ikhlas and al-Zalzala.
rows.anchor: وهذا العدل إما أن يكون في المعاني ، وإما أن يكون تفضيلا من الله تعالى لا يعلل

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet assigned al-Fatiha thirty more merits than other speech.
rows.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A further Prophetic report assigns twenty merits to saying la ilaha illa Allah and thirty to saying al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin.
rows.anchor: وورد حديث آخر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The merit comparison concerns believers seeking reward: al-hamdu combines praise with the monotheism contained in la ilaha illa Allah, while the latter contains monotheism alone.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله : { الحمد لله } في ضمنها التوحيد الذي هو معنى لا إله إلا الله ، ففي قوله توحيد وحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In their role of warding off unbelief and association, la ilaha illa Allah is superior; the Prophet called it the best statement he and earlier prophets had uttered.
rows.anchor: أفضل ما قلته أنا والنبيون من قبلي

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
rows.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq calls the basmala the crowns of the surahs.
rows.anchor: روي عن جعفر بن محمد الصادق رضي الله عنه أنه قال : البسملة تيجان السور

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a man cursed Satan in the Prophet's presence, the Prophet said this magnified Satan and instructed him to say the basmala, which makes Satan shrink smaller than a fly.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «لا تقل ذلك فإنه يتعاظم عنده ولكن قل بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فإنه يصغر حتى يصير أقل

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali b. al-Husayn interprets the turning away in 17:46 when the Lord is mentioned alone as occurring when one says the basmala.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن الحسين رضي الله عنه في تفسير قوله تعالى { وإذا ذكرت ربك في القرآن وحده ولوا على أدبارهم نفورا } قال معناه إذا قلت بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jabir says that when he told the Prophet he opened prayer with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin, the Prophet told him to say the basmala.
rows.anchor: وروي عن جابر بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet prayer and recited the basmala aloud.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says that, on their face, the Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports imply the basmala is an ayah of al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وهذان الحديثان يقتضيان أنها آية من الحمد

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: An authentic report has the Prophet ask Ubayy to recite the surah; Ubayy begins with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin and continues to its end, without the basmala.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي بن كعب الصحيح إذ قال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الله تعالى في الحديث القدسي
rows.claim: The sound hadith qudsi describing prayer as divided between God and the servant quotes the servant beginning with al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin, not the basmala.
rows.anchor: ويرده الحديث الصحيح بقوله عز وجل { قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي ، يقول العبد الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No record says the Prophet or Abu Bakr, Umar or Uthman recited the basmala in prayer.
rows.anchor: ويرده أنه لم يحفظ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا عن أبي بكر ولا عن عمر ولا عثمان رضي الله عنهم أنهم قرؤوا في صلاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is counted as seven verses by consensus, apart from the anomalous report that al-Husayn al-Ju'fi counted six.
rows.anchor: الإجماع أنها سبع آيات إلا ما روي عن حسين الجعفي أنها ست آيات وهذا شاذ لا يعول عليه

rows.speaker: حسين الجعفي
rows.claim: Al-Husayn al-Ju'fi reportedly counts six verses in al-Fatiha; Ibn Atiyya calls this anomalous and unreliable.
rows.anchor: إلا ما روي عن حسين الجعفي أنها ست آيات وهذا شاذ لا يعول عليه

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Amr b. Ubayd makes iyyaka na'budu a separate verse, yielding eight; Ibn Atiyya also calls this anomalous.
rows.anchor: روي عن عمرو بن عبيد أنه جعل { إياك نعبد } آية ، فهي على عده ثماني آيات ، وهذا أيضا شاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God gave the Prophet seven oft-repeated verses in 15:87 settles the verse-count question.
rows.anchor: وقول الله تعالى { ولقد آتيناك سبعا من المثاني } هو الفصل في ذلك

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i counts the basmala as a verse of al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: والشافعي رحمه الله يعد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية من الحمد

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة
rows.claim: Many Meccan and Kufan reciters do not count an'amta alayhim as a verse.
rows.anchor: وكثير من قراء مكة والكوفة لا يعدون { أنعمت عليهم }

rows.speaker: مالك، وأبو حنيفة، وجمهور الفقهاء والقراء
rows.claim: Malik, Abu Hanifa and the majority of jurists and reciters do not count the basmala as a verse.
rows.anchor: ومالك رحمه الله وأبو حنيفة وجمهور الفقهاء والقراء لا يعدون البسملة آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If sound, the Jabir and Abu Hurayra reports can be understood as lessons: the Prophet saw them rehearsing prayer outside prayer and taught the basmala for that reason, not because it was a verse.
rows.anchor: والذي يحتمله عندي حديث جابر وأبي هريرة إذا صحا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى قراءة جابر وحكايته أمر الصلاة قراءة في غير صلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not include the basmala in his exchange with Ubayy because he was identifying the special surah and its virtue, whereas that purpose was absent in the instructional exchanges with Jabir and Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: ولم يفعل ذلك مع أبي لأنه قصد تخصيص السورة ووسمها من الفضل بما لها ، فلم يدخل معها ما ليس منها

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak holds that the basmala is a verse in every surah; Ibn Atiyya calls this an anomalous view rejected by others.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المبارك : إن البسملة آية في كل سورة وهذا قول شاذ رد الناس عليه

rows.speaker: الشعبي والأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi and al-A'mash report a progression in the Prophet's written basmala: first Bismika Allahumma, then Bismillah, then Bismillah al-Rahman, and after 27:30 the full formula.
rows.anchor: وروى الشعبي والأعمش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يكتب

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: Amr b. Shurahbil reports that Gabriel first came to the Prophet saying, “Say: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate.”
rows.anchor: وروى عمرو بن شرحبيل أن جبريل أول ما جاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له قل بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the first thing Gabriel brought down was the basmala.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن أول ما نزل به جبريل بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: خديجة عن ورقة
rows.claim: In some versions of Khadija's taking the Prophet to Waraqa, Gabriel first tells the Prophet to say the basmala; the Prophet says it, then Gabriel commands him to read, and he replies that he cannot read.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض طرق حديث خديجة وحملها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى ورقة

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some say the nineteen letters of the basmala correspond one by one to the nineteen keepers of Hell in 74:30, whose repeated basmala gives them strength.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض الناس : إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the letter-count explanation a playful exegetical conceit, not sound scholarship.
rows.anchor: وهذه من ملح التفسير وليست من متين العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares that numerology with claims that the Night of Decree is the twenty-seventh night because of a word in its surah, and that thirty-some angels rushed to record a thirty-some-letter praise formula.
rows.anchor: وهي نظير قولهم في ليلة القدر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A similar letter-count claim says thirty-some angels competed to record “Our Lord, to You belongs praise, abundant, good and blessed praise”; Ibn Atiyya presents it as the same sort of numerology.
rows.anchor: ونظير قولهم في عدد الملائكة الذين ابتدروا قول القائل

rows.speaker: نحاة البصرة
rows.claim: Basran grammarians attach the preposition bi- to an implied noun such as ibtida'i, mustaqirr or thabit, making the whole basmala nominative in their analysis.
rows.anchor: والباء في بسم الله متعلقة عند نحاة البصرة

rows.speaker: نحاة الكوفة
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians attach bi- to an implied verb, “I begin,” and parse the basmala as accusative.
rows.anchor: وعند نحاة الكوفة بفعل تقديره : ابتدأت

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Sibawayh apparently attaches bi- to a noun, yet treats the phrase as accusative through attachment to thabit or mustaqirr, like Zayd is in the house.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من مذهب سيبويه أن الباء متعلقة باسم كما تقدم . وبسم الله في موضع نصب تعلقا بثابت أو مستقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra on bi- is explained as matching its grammatical action, because it governs nouns, or to distinguish it from particles that can also be nouns.
rows.anchor: وكسرت باء الجر ليناسب لفظها عملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's use of kaf is cited as an example of a particle that can function as a noun, motivating a distinctive genitive mark for bi-.
rows.anchor: أو ليفرق بينها وبين ما قد يكون من الحروف اسما نحو الكاف في قول الأعشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is omitted from the written basmala for brevity and ease because the phrase is so frequently used.
rows.anchor: وحذفت الألف من بسم الله في الخط اختصارا وتخفيفا لكثرة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: الكسائي وسعيد الأخفش، ويحيى بن زياد
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Sa'id al-Akhfash omit the alif in bism al-Rahman and bism al-Qahir; Yahya b. Ziyad says omission applies only with Allah because that phrase is especially frequent. Ibn Atiyya says the alif remains with other names.
rows.anchor: فقال الكسائي وسعيد الأخفش يحذف الألف

rows.speaker: نحاة البصرة
rows.claim: Basran grammarians derive ism from sumuww, elevation, from sama yasmu; the form is associated with either damma or kasra in the initial consonant.
rows.anchor: وهو عند البصريين مشتق من السمو ، يقال سما يسمو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The diminutive sumayy, plural asma', and plural-of-plural asami support the Basran etymology; a poetic form simahu is also cited.
rows.anchor: وإنما استدل على هذا الأصل الذي ذكرناه

rows.speaker: نحاة الكوفة
rows.claim: Kufans derive ism from wasm, a mark, since a name marks its bearer; Ibn Atiyya says this sense is apt but morphology counters it, since the forms should be wasim and awsām.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون : أصل اسم وسم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the name-and-named question is not appropriate here and criticizes theologians for debating it and similar questions.
rows.anchor: فقال الطبري رحمه الله : إنه ليس بموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A name such as Zayd or lion can mean its referent, as in Zayd stands, or the word itself, as in lion has three letters; only in the first use does the name mean the named.
rows.anchor: الاسم كزيد وأسد وفرس قد يرد في الكلام

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
rows.claim: Many scholars take name to mean the named essence in 87:1, 55:78 and 53:23; they cite Labid's line about the name of peace as a greeting.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا حمل أكثر أهل العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More commonly, ism denotes the verbal name itself: examples include Adam being taught the names, the hadith of God's ninety-nine names, and grammarians' technical usage.
rows.anchor: وقد يجري اسم في اللغة مجرى ذات العبارة وهو الأكثر من استعمالها فمنه قوله تعالى { وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها }

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: When asked whether the name is the named, Malik answered that it is neither it nor other than it, meaning this is not true in every context.
rows.anchor: ومر بي أن مالكا رحمه الله سئل عن الاسم أهو المسمى فقال ليس به ولا هو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is the most striking and frequently used of God's names, usually preceding the others, which generally function as attributes.
rows.anchor: أبهر أسماء الله تعالى وأكثرها استعمالا

rows.speaker: فرقة من أهل العلم
rows.claim: One group of scholars treats Allah as an un-derived proper name, with alif-lam integral to the name rather than a marker of definiteness.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة من أهل العلم هو اسم مرتجل لا اشتقاق له من فعل وإنما هو اسم موضوع له تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: كثير من أهل العلم
rows.claim: Many scholars derive Allah from alaha, worship, or ta'allaha, devotion; Ibn Abbas and others gloss the Qur'anic wa-alihatak in 7:127 as your worship.
rows.anchor: وذهب كثير من أهل العلم إلى أنه مشتق من أله الرجل إذا عبد وتأله إذا تنسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three accounts explain the change from ilah to Allah: irregular loss of hamza before alif-lam, alif-lam added to ilah with hamza-vowel transfer and lam assimilation, or an original lah; Ibn Atiyya favors the first.
rows.anchor: فقيل حذفت الهمزة حذفا على غير قياس

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says the original was ilah or walah, with hamza substituted for waw as in ishaḥ/wishaḥ and isadah/wisadah.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الخليل أن أصل إله ولاه وأن الهمزة مبدلة من واو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account derives the word from walah, bewilderment: intellects are bewildered by the realities of God's attributes and by thought about knowing Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أصل الكلمة ولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final alif of Allah is said to be omitted to distinguish its script from al-Lat, for ease, or as a dialect form; Ibn al-A'rabi's verse is cited for the latter.
rows.anchor: وحذفت الألف الأخيرة من الله لئلا يشكل بخط اللات ، وقيل طرحت تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman is an intensive form from mercy, reaching its utmost limit and belonging specifically to God; rahim exceeds rahim as a description of one who showed mercy once, while al-Rahman marks the utmost degree.
rows.anchor: والرحمن صفة مبالغة من الرحمة ومعناها أنه انتهى إلى غاية الرحمة

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some say al-Rahman and al-Rahim share the same meaning and root, like nadman and nadim, with one form more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الناس : الرحمن الرحيم بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: العرزمي
rows.claim: Al-Arzami explains al-Rahman as mercy to all creation through rain, senses and general blessings, and al-Rahim as mercy to believers through guidance and kindness.
rows.anchor: أن العرزمي قال : معناه : الرحمن

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Ibn Mas'ud report the Prophet explaining al-Rahman as merciful in this world and the next, al-Rahim as merciful in the next world.
rows.anchor: أن أبا سعيد الخدري وابن مسعود رويا

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says al-Rahman names God's mercy in all its kinds and is exclusive to Him, while al-Rahim is for believers, as 33:43 says; Ibn Atiyya says the readings reinforce one another.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي : الرحمن اسم عام

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Ata al-Khurasani says God paired al-Rahman with al-Rahim after Musaylima adopted the name al-Rahman, making the combination exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء الخراساني : كان الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects Ata's account as weak: the basmala preceded Musaylima's rise, and Musaylima's use of the name did not become established.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ضعيف لأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم كان قبل أن ينجم أمر مسيلمة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Arabs did not know or use al-Rahman, citing their question in 25:60 about what al-Rahman is.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم : إن العرب كانت لا تعرف لفظة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects that lexical claim: the Arabs objected to identifying the deity they were ordered to worship, not to the word al-Rahman itself.
rows.anchor: وإنما وقفت العرب على تعيين الإله الذي أمروا بالسجود له لا على نفس اللفظة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Umm Salama says the Prophet paused on the sukun of rahim, stopped there, and began al-hamd with a hamzat al-qat'; some Kufans recited this way.
rows.anchor: فروي عن أم سلمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: Most reciters read al-rahimi l-hamdu with the genitive ending and connect the alif of al-hamd.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس { الرحيمِ الْحَمْد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected reading can be explained by positing a pause on a silent mim, then voicing it to avoid adjacent sukun letters without treating the hamza of al as cut; Ibn Atiyya finds the simpler account more concise.
rows.anchor: ومن شاء أن يقدر أنه أسكن الميم ثم لما وصل حركها للالتقاء ولم يعتد بألف الوصل فذلك سائغ والأول أخصر

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reports an Arab reading al-rahima al-hamdu with a fatḥa on mim and a connected alif, explained by transferring the hamza's vowel to the mim after elision.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن بعض العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya knows no one who transmitted al-Kisa'i's form as a recognized reading; it matches Yahya b. Ziyad's grammatical analysis of Alif Lam Mim Allah.
rows.anchor: ولم ترو هذه قراءةً عن أحد فيما علمت
